# A match is checked into an if/else-if chain or a chain of ternaries, so every
# target runs it as the if or the ternary it is. The program covers a view
# body's match, an expression match, an option, the headless form, and a
# subject that calls -- made once where a statement can hold it, and asserted
# so by counting the calls.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '6 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '6 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '6 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '6 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '6 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '6 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
// `match` picks the first arm whose pattern equals its subject. An arm is a
// block where a statement goes and `pattern => expr` where a value does, the
// two forms a func has. A pattern is a constant or `null`; a bare enum member
// resolves against the subject's type, commas give an arm several patterns,
// and `else` is the arm that runs when no other did. Every match is
// exhaustive.

import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"

enum Status { active, inactive, pending }

component panel node {
    var status Status = pending
    var maybe option[Status] = null
    var n = 0

    // In a view body: a node in an arm is rendered while that arm is taken.
    match status {
        active { text #on(value="on") }
        pending, inactive { text #off(value="not on") }
    }

    // An expression: every member is covered, so no else.
    text #label(value=match status {
        active => "on"
        pending => "waiting"
        inactive => "off"
    })

    // An option: null is one more case to cover.
    text #shown(value=match maybe {
        null => "none"
        active => "on"
        else => "not on"
    })

    // Headless: each arm is a condition, tested in order.
    text #size(value=match {
        n > 10 => "big"
        n > 0 => "small"
        else => "none"
    })

    var picked = ""
    var calls = 0

    func count() Status {
        calls = calls + 1
        return status
    }

    // An expression match on a call: the call is made once, not per arm.
    button #pick(text="Pick", @click {
        picked = match count() {
            active => "a"
            inactive => "i"
            else => "p"
        }
    })

    button #step(text="Step", @click {
        // In a handler: a subject that is not a plain read is evaluated once.
        match next(status) {
            active { n = n + 1 }
            else {}
        }
        status = next(status)
    })
}

const func next(s Status) => match s {
    active => Status.inactive
    inactive => pending
    pending => active
}

var bumps = 0

func bump(s Status) Status {
    bumps = bumps + 1
    return s
}

// An expression body is the statement `return …`, so it binds its subject too.
func label(s Status) => match bump(s) {
    active => "on"
    else => "off"
}

func describe(n int) string {
    match n {
        0 { return "zero" }
        1, 2, 3 { return "few" }
        else { return "many" }
    }
}

func testViewArm(t Test, c panel) {
    t.assert(c.on == null)
    t.assert(c.off != null)
    t.assert(c.label.value == "waiting")
}

func testOption(t Test, c panel) {
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "none")
    c.maybe = active
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "on")
    c.maybe = pending
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "not on")
}

func testHeadless(t Test, c panel) {
    t.assert(c.size.value == "none")
    c.n = 4
    t.assert(c.size.value == "small")
    c.n = 11
    t.assert(c.size.value == "big")
}

func testHandler(t Test, c panel) {
    c.step.click()
    t.assert(c.status == active)
    t.assert(c.n == 1)
    t.assert(c.on != null)
    t.assert(c.label.value == "on")
}

func testSubjectOnce(t Test, c panel) {
    c.pick.click()
    t.assert(c.picked == "p")
    t.assert(c.calls == 1)
    t.assert(label(Status.active) == "on")
    t.assert(bumps == 1)
}

func testFunc(t Test) {
    t.assert(describe(0) == "zero")
    t.assert(describe(2) == "few")
    t.assert(describe(9) == "many")
    t.assert(next(pending) == active)
}

window {
    panel
}
